text.p: Eagle-Picher Industries Inc said on Friday that its Plan of Reorganization became effective as of November 29, 1996 to bring the company out of bankruptcy and leave current equity holders with nothing.

In the initial distribution under the plan, $250 million in principal of 10-year debentures of the reorganized company and all of the reorganized company's shares were transferred to a trust to resolve asbestos and lead-related personal injury claims, the company said.

The trust also received about $50 million cash, $18 million of three-year notes of the reorganized company and approximately $69 million in principal amount of other notes which mature in 1998, Eagle-Picher.
The company's plan precludes holders of present and future asbestos or asbestos-related claims from pursuing them against the reorganized company, Eagle-Picher said.
Under the plan, asbestos-related property damage claims asserted against the company will be resolved by a separate trust that will get $3 million under the reorganization, Eagle-Picher said.

Eagle-Picher said it expects that holders of prepetition general unsecured claims (other than asbestos and lead-related claims) will receive consideration valued at about 37 percent of their allowed claims.
Half of those claims will be paid in cash and the other half in three-year notes, Eagle-Picher said.

Eagle-Picher entered into a new unsecured $60 million revolving credit facility with a group of banks, it said. The facility has a three-year term and can be utilized for both cash borrowings and for the issuance of letters of credit, the company said.
